title: 'Flow Gently, Sweet Rhythm' as theme and the Kirby compositions
summary: She explains the signature tune and how Charlie Shavers wrote most of the band's originals, linking to 'Opus de Funk'-like themes.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: There's a title listed here, 'Flow Gently Sweet Rhythm,' which we had discussed. And 'Flow Gently Sweet Rhythm' -- there was a theme that the orchestra used at the time.
Yeah. That was a signature tune.
Right. When it was originally written, it was called 'Let's Begin Again.' It was one of those BMI tunes that were written during the ASCAP-BMI situation.

And, of course, under the music, there was commentary there. Originally when we did the show, Canada Lee did the commentary. And on that particular album on this particular date, Canada Lee was no longer with us either.
And Jack Walker did the commentary.
He was a well-known --

That's right. I remember it's a side of Milt Jackson or Horace Silver composition recorded, I think, in the late 40's under the title "Opus de Funk," on the Savoy label if I'm not mistaken.
